text:
Tyler Bertuzzi scored 32 goals for Chicago last season. Through 18 games this year he has 2, and none in his last ten. The Chicago Sun-Times asked the obvious question this week ("Why Tyler Bertuzzi's goal-scoring has disappeared for Blackhawks this season"), and our numbers give a split answer.

Part of it is luck. With him on the ice, the Blackhawks have scored 6.0 fewer goals than their chances deserve, and a shortfall like that usually swings back. Part of it is real: his individual expected goals (the quality of the chances he gets himself) are down to 0.67 per 60 from 1.25 last season, and Chicago gets only 41% of the expected goals when he's on at five on five.

Context helps him. Evolving-Hockey rated him 20th among 401 forwards last season by wins above replacement and noted he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league. He's still the net-front body on the first power-play unit, per The Athletic's Scott Powers. Our projection has him finishing near 19 goals. We'd expect the chances to come back before the goals do, so watch how often he gets to the slot.
headline: Where did Tyler Bertuzzi's goals go?
